explainer.lead: The viscosity solution is a generalization of what it means to solve a partial differential equation, introduced in the early 1980s by Pierre-Louis Lions and Michael G. Crandall. It matters because it is the natural solution concept for many PDE applications where classical solutions do not apply.

tiers.eli5: Sometimes the usual rules for solving a maths equation break down, so people agreed on a looser rule for what counts as an answer—and that looser rule turns out to be the right one for many real problems.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers and applied mathematicians use viscosity solutions when working with equations from dynamic programming, differential games, or front evolution. A pitfall is assuming a classical solution exists or applies where only the viscosity concept is appropriate.
tiers.paperLevel: A viscosity solution is a generalized notion of solution to a partial differential equation, defined as a generalization of the classical solution concept. It is the natural concept for first-order equations such as Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman and Hamilton–Jacobi–Isaacs and for front evolution problems, as well as for second-order equations. Its limits follow from being a generalized concept rather than a classical one.

explainer.example: A dynamic programming problem formulated as a Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation is solved in the viscosity sense when no classical solution is available.
